clue.text: Having lost case, simply with no case to lose

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order
the case of a word is its outer pair of letters, so the word simply loses its first and last

explanation.surface: A lawyer who has lost the brief now has simply no case left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no case' strips SIMPLY to IMPL; 'lost' shuffles CASE plus IMPL. 'Having' is a link, and the repeated 'case' makes the surface feel like legal talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to put it down and fail to find it, a mild synonym for losing it.

clue.text: Setters' pleasure trips no longer starting with a thematic dash

explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Morse code: a single dash is T, so TOURS without its opening T is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters writing collectively would call what belongs to them 'ours', the first person plural possessive.

clue.text: German city's missing hotel by river, previously knocked down

missing tells us a letter has gone from the city's name

parts.note: Hanover is a city in Germany
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A German city lacks a hotel beside its river, which was demolished earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'previously' puts R before ANOVER, Hanover with its H 'missing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over someone in a vehicle is to knock them down.

clue.text: Pull up after taking the lead from Steve Cram

the lead of a word is its opening letter, here of the name Steve
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls up after Steve Cram, the British middle-distance runner, takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British middle-distance runner, so 'Cram' looks like part of the name, yet it is the definition. 'up' reverses the pull, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To swot is British slang for studying hard, just as to cram is to study intensively before an exam.

clue.text: Element nitrogen is missing from compound number 1

is missing from says the nitrogen letter is removed from the mixed pool

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that nitrogen is absent from compound number one.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER plus I, with N 'missing from' them, leaves UMBERI, which 'compound' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Erbium is a chemical element, one of the rare-earth metals.

clue.text: Pull bat away regularly after proper bloomer

parts.note: prim means primly proper

indicators.note: taking letters away at regular intervals leaves every other letter of pull bat

explanation.surface: A cricketer is told to pull the bat away regularly after a proper blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flowering plant. 'away regularly' drops P, L, B, T to leave ULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A primula is a flowering plant, such as a primrose, and a flower is a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Portrait's head isn't the Queen, according to artist

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.definitionFit: A painter is an artist who works in paint.

clue.text: Uncanny, Dot (single) making right move twice in highly-strung state

indicators.note: the letter moves two places to the right within the word

parts.note: weird means uncanny
in Morse code, the theme, a single dot is the letter E

explanation.surface: A strange woman named Dot, who is single, keeps moving house and is a bundle of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: Dot reads as a woman's name, but in Morse a lone dot is E. In WEIRD the E shifts two places right.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wired is tense and jumpy, keyed up as if by electricity, so in a highly-strung state.

clue.text: Read out, say, writing that's depressingly dull in literary terms

indicators.note: out signals that the word read is put out of its usual order

explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges READ to DREA; the 'three Rs' are reading, writing and arithmetic, so writing gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic, old-fashioned form of dreary, used mainly in literature for gloomy and dull.

clue.text: Setter's power as mischief-maker

P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small mischievous sprite, hence a naughty child who causes trouble.

clue.text: His older TV's repair is not long-lasting

indicators.note: repairing a set puts its parts back together, here in a new order

explanation.surface: His old television keeps needing repairs and doesn't last long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges HISOLDERTV; the 's after TV is just 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something short-lived has a brief existence, the opposite of enduring.

clue.text: Guy more than once needing to make a dash for it, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the letters are what we hear when they are spoken

parts.words: more than once needing to make a dash for it
parts.note: a dash in Morse is the letter T, and needing it more than once gives the plural Ts

explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to mock or ridicule them, so to tease them.

clue.text: Burst of letters from higher up, thematically

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A burst of letters arrives from somewhere higher up, in keeping with the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst out violently, as a volcano does.

clue.text: Recording that male setter's given 6D 10 things

he is a male pronoun
the setter refers to himself as me
6 Down is PAINTER, and an RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.walkthrough: '6D' points to PAINTER, here RA (Royal Academician); '10' points to SHORT-LIVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that last only a short time, such as tickets and flyers kept as collectables.

clue.text: Stink is about fine? That's nonsense

OK means fine

clue.text: Stopped talking and did postprandial chore?

after a meal, someone dries up the washed dishes

explanation.definitionFit: Drying up means both falling silent mid-speech and wiping dishes dry after washing up.

clue.text: Excessive as cost might be, if broadcaster under influence of a drug?

explanation.walkthrough: SKY is a British satellite television broadcaster.

clue.text: Very strong man in Cheers, playing university lecturer

clue.text: Suggest a possible case for secret police

indicators.note: the words act as a case holding the answer inside them

explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Stuck bug on leads of peripheral electronic devices? That's about right

indicators.note: leads are the front ends, so the first letters of each word

clue.text: Creative person gets home by taking second north out of IOW town

out of marks the removal from the town name

clue.text: Very much recovered at last, after turning up gas

in a down clue, turning up means the word is read upwards, so reversed

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word recovered

clue.text: Wasted time during last two-thirds of second half? It makes you sick!

half takes the first half of the word second
wasted suggests the word time is ruined, so rearranged

clue.text: Manners shown by Dr. Dre? Not at first, in today's theme …

clue.text: Unusually large pets receiving hard-7 messages?

clue.text: Gregory's car registration? Sydney's, actually
